title: 2003 shooting still troubles community, chief says
article: First Nations and the RCMP must come up with a better system for investigating controversial incidents that involve aboriginal people, say leaders of the First Nations Summit.

Members of the Namgis First Nation in Alert Bay are unable to heal following the February 2003 dispute that ended with Lorraine Moon (also known as Lorraine Jacobson) being shot dead by RCMP Const. Russ Chanin.
They feel it was unacceptable for the RCMP to head the investigation, Chief Doug Kelly of the First Nations Summit political executive said Saturday.
"We find it totally unacceptable that the RCMP have been in charge of conducting the investigation into a death resulting from an RCMP officer's actions," he said.

"It would have been much more appropriate to have conducted a totally independent and unbiased investigation which would allow for a full disclosure of evidence and closure for Ms. Jacobson's family and the members of the surrounding First Nations communities."
The RCMP also controlled too much of the evidence given to the coroner's jury at this week's inquest, said Namgis Chief William Cranmer.
"They provided almost all the evidence and many of the witnesses. Even the expert was an RCMP officer. Where is the independence?"
Alert Bay RCMP referred calls about the Moon case to a Port Alberni RCMP staff sergeant, who could not be contacted Saturday.
Cranmer said First Nations trust in the police is threatened when, after an RCMP officer kills an aboriginal person, the RCMP investigates the death to see if criminal charges should be laid.
"The First Nations are calling on the federal and provincial governments to change the current system and provide for independent inquiries when it is the RCMP which is being investigated," he said.

Kelly said the First Nations Summit is calling on Assembly of First Nations Chief Phil Fontaine and regional Chief Shawn Atleo to help negotiate a B.C. First Nations/RCMP protocol to address such issues.
A national protocol was negotiated recently, but a separate one is needed for the Pacific Region, he said.
The protocol could also serve as a road map for situations such as clashes in Gold River between the Mowachaht/Muchalaht and fisheries officers, Kelly said.
"It is something which is absolutely necessary," he said.
"The history of First Nations and the RCMP is not a healthy one. It is built on many past acts of injustice and unfair treatment."
Chanin told the inquest that he felt he had to intervene after being called to Moon's home where she was threatening to kill two men.
Moon, 40, then threatened him with a butcher's knife, he said.
The shooting was investigated by the Courtenay RCMP major crimes unit, but no criminal charges were laid.
The inquest jury recommended that RCMP officers in B.C. should receive extensive conflict resolution training.
Recommendations for the RCMP detachment in Alert Bay included keeping open radio contact to a second officer when an officer is called out to a disturbance.
